dailyRead: The de-escalation the whole book was warned about is deepening, and the oil premium keeps unwinding. The US and Iran have now paused strikes for a second straight day and are moving back toward interim-ceasefire talks, while Iran holds Strait of Hormuz discussions with Saudi Arabia and Oman - an initial framework to extend the truce and reopen the strait is reported, though challenges remain. Crude fell a second leg, WTI down ~4% to ~$79 (Brent ~$86.6), compounded by a fresh US inventory build. Every oil-linked leg extends: CAD's terms-of-trade premium is gutted further (the clearest loser), gold and silver bled toward $4,030 / $57.5 off the haven bid, and the yen gets a fundamental oil-relief tailwind - though USD/JPY still sits ~163.8 because the dollar is firm into the Fed. The story is now policy, not oil: tomorrow (Wed Jul 29) delivers a twin binary - the FOMC (CME ~65% hold / ~35% hike, up from ~16% on Jul 23; September ~82% priced) AND Australia Q2 CPI (consensus trimmed mean ~3.7-3.8%). Cleanest lean stays USD/CAD LONG (HIGH); USOIL SHORT (MED); XAU/XAG RANGE (short tilt); and last week's cleanest trade, CAD/JPY LONG, is dead - RANGE (short tilt). The caveat that caps the whole de-escalation trade: the pause is not a signed deal, so a breakdown re-arms every oil leg in a single session.

geopolitics: De-escalation is deepening, and the oil trade is one-way down. The US and Iran have now paused strikes for a second straight day and are moving back toward interim-ceasefire talks, while Iran holds Strait of Hormuz discussions with Saudi Arabia and Oman; an initial framework to extend the truce and reopen the strait is reported, though challenges remain. Crude, which last week printed the cycle high on the strike nights, fell a second leg - WTI down ~4% to ~$79 (Brent ~$86.6) - compounded by a fresh US inventory build. The crucial caveat: the pause is NOT a signed deal, so the marginal headline risk still runs both ways. FX transmission: (1) CAD is the clearest loser - the terms-of-trade premium that made it last week's winner keeps draining with crude near $79 and no domestic hawkish leg to replace it; USD/CAD LONG (HIGH) is the cleanest expression. (2) The JPY gets more fundamental relief - the energy importer benefits most, and BoJ Jul 31 (trend 1.9%) keeps the hawks armed even on a hold - but spot still ~163.8 as the dollar is firm into the Fed. (3) The USD's bid rotates from haven to policy - hike odds ~35% (Sept ~82%); DXY long tilt. (4) Gold and silver bled off the haven bid toward $4,030 / $57.5 - XAU/XAG RANGE (short tilt). (5) NZD and GBP lose their fuel-CPI engine as the petrol pass-through stops renewing, softening both forward paths. (6) The DAX gets an energy-cost tailwind - GER40 leans long. Every oil-linked leg keys off the same binary - and today it extended to the downside. If the US-Iran pause breaks down, it all snaps back.
